title: An open section is also closed
statement:
Let $p:V\to S$ be a
separated morphism and
$s:S\hookrightarrow V$ an
open immersion satisfying
$p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$. Its image is open and closed in
$V$, and the decomposition
$V=s(S)\amalg(V\setminus s(S))$ is a decomposition into open
subschemes.

proof.text: The identity of $S$ is a closed immersion: its underlying map is a homeomorphism onto the whole (closed) space and its map on structure sheaves is the identity, hence surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $p$ is separated and $p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite] with $T=S$ and $r=s$ to conclude that $s$ is a closed immersion. Its image $U=s(S)$ is therefore closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; it is open, and $S$ is isomorphic to the open subscheme $(U,\mathcal O_V|_U)$, by the hypothesis and [def-weil-open-immersion].

Let $W=V\setminus U$. Since $U$ is closed, $W$ is open and has its open-subscheme structure $(W,\mathcal O_V|_W)$. The equalities $U\cap W=\varnothing$ and $U\cup W=V$ follow from the definition of complement. Thus the two open subschemes form a disjoint open cover of $V$. On each member the map to $V$ is the inclusion and the structure sheaf is its restriction; the inverse on underlying spaces sends each point to its unique member of the cover and is continuous because both members are open. For each open $A\subseteq V$, the sheaf axiom for the disjoint cover gives $\mathcal O_V(A)\cong\mathcal O_V(A\cap U)\times\mathcal O_V(A\cap W)$, compatibly with restriction, so the inclusion map is also an isomorphism on structure sheaves. This identifies their disjoint union with $V$, giving $V=s(S)\amalg(V\setminus s(S))$.
